title: Inbound-burst auto-detection + cadence-revert recommendation signal — close the 'quiet-period throttle has no automated un-throttle' gap surfaced by the pre-active-period readiness audit (DIRECTIVE-20260628-002 / PROP-116 Candidate C)
addresses_weak_link: WL-2 (rank-1) in monitor/tinker/readiness-audits/pre-active-period-2026-06-28.md; collapses recovery latency for WL-1 (curmudgeon HOL) and WL-4 (verify paused)
problem_statement: The 2026-06-23 quiet-period sweep throttled analyst, curmudgeon, and decider to 1 run/day and PAUSED curmudgeon-verify (enabled:false). Each throttle's revert is documented as MANUAL and operator-triggered ('REVERT … if dome breaks drought / work volume returns'; 'Re-enable when verify-class items appear'). Nothing in the pipeline detects an inbound burst and re-escalates. The poller already detects new WINs (writes status.json + monitor/changes/) but touches no cadence. Result under a 3-WIN drought-break: curmudgeon reviews 1 fresh WIN/run (curmudgeon.md:72,160; win-new not batchable curmudgeon.md:243 gate5) at 1 run/day → the burst crawls for ~5-6 days for first-review+first-patch, versus ~1 day at reverted 3-slot cadence. The throughput collapse is real and deterministic; the recovery is entirely detection-latency-bound.
design_principles: RECOMMEND, NEVER AUTO-FLIP. The PROP emits a loud, structured signal recommending the specific cron reverts; a human (or a future, separately-approved enforce phase) actually flips crons. This preserves operator control and respects DIRECTIVE-20260628-001's rejection of tinker-initiated throttle changes — by only ever recommending UP-throttle in response to measured inbound load, never down-throttle.

PRIMARY DETECTOR = POLLER (earliest signal, same detection cycle). FALLBACK DETECTOR = TINKER backlog-trend pre-flight (PROP-030), which already runs every tinker run and already writes latest-tinker-summary.txt that the operator reads each morning. Two detectors because poller is Sonnet/once-daily and could itself be slow under burst; tinker is the safety net with <=24h latency.

CONSERVATIVE THRESHOLD. Fire on >=2 new WINs detected in one poll OR priority-queue depth of unreviewed win-new items >=2 OR new-wins/ backlog >=2. Single-WIN inbound is normal quiet-period work and must NOT fire (avoids false-alarm cron churn).
NO NEW STATE-FILE OWNERSHIP DISPUTES. The signal is an HNOTE (dual-write per CLAUDE.md Human Notes Rule) + a summary line. No new owned file, no build.js OWNERSHIP / workspace-sync NEVER_PUSH change.

detector_A_poller.where: poller.md, after the change-classification step that already counts new dome WINs
detector_A_poller.logic: Compute new_win_delta = dome_win_count(status.json, freshly polled) - len(data/wins.json from GitHub raw). If new_win_delta >= 2, write a burst-signal HNOTE to monitor/decisions/human-notes.json (dual-write FUSE+clone) with action:'recommend_cadence_revert', a fields block listing the recommended reverts (dome-curmudgeon 0 2,6,10 ; dome-analyst 0 1,5,9 ; dome-decider 0 3,7,11 ; re-enable dome-curmudgeon-verify), the measured new_win_delta, and detected_at. Idempotency: guard on an existing pending HNOTE with the same action AND new_win_delta within the same UTC day (do not spam one HNOTE per poll).
detector_A_poller.no_op_path: new_win_delta < 2 → no HNOTE, no behavior change. Pure additive read + conditional write.

detector_B_tinker_fallback.where: tinker backlog-trend pre-flight (this prompt, the PROP-030 metrics block) — ADDITIVE metric only
detector_B_tinker_fallback.logic: Add metric inbound_burst_winnew_unreviewed = count of priority-queue.json items with target_type=='win-new' that have no matching review file in monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/. If >=2, emit a findings[] object category='inbound-burst' severity='major' AND write a one-line escalation to latest-tinker-summary.txt recommending the same cron reverts. This is the safety net if detector_A (poller) missed or was slow.
detector_B_tinker_fallback.no_op_path: metric < 2 → metric still recorded in queue-history.jsonl for trend, no finding.

proposed_mechanism.operator_consumption: Operator sees the HNOTE (decider surfaces pending human-notes) and/or the tinker summary line, and flips the crons via update_scheduled_task. Optional future enforce-phase (SEPARATE PROP, explicitly not in scope here) could let an empowered agent flip the crons after an approval HNOTE — deliberately deferred so the first version cannot mis-fire a cron flip.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: When >=2 new WINs are detected in a single poll, a burst-signal HNOTE with action:'recommend_cadence_revert' appears in monitor/decisions/human-notes.json (both FUSE and git), listing the four specific recommended cron reverts and the measured new_win_delta.
AC2: When <2 new WINs are detected, NO burst HNOTE is written and no cadence behavior changes (verified by a single-WIN onboarding leaving human-notes.json burst-HNOTE-free).
AC3: Idempotency — repeated polls on the same burst-day do not append duplicate burst HNOTEs (guarded by same-action + same-day check).

AC4: tinker's queue-history.jsonl gains an inbound_burst_winnew_unreviewed metric every run; when >=2 it produces a findings[] category='inbound-burst' AND a latest-tinker-summary.txt escalation line.
AC5: No cron is ever flipped automatically by this PROP. (Verified by code-read: the only writes are HNOTE + summary line + metric.)
AC6: No change to build.js OWNERSHIP or workspace-sync NEVER_PUSH (the HNOTE and summary are already-classified surfaces).

verification_pattern.note: Multi-agent prompt change (poller + tinker) — not a single mechanical script, so a clean exit-0 verification_pattern is not fully expressible until implemented. Manual acceptance: simulate by temporarily setting a 2-WIN delta in a scratch status.json and confirming AC1/AC2/AC3 in a dry-run, then confirm AC4 by injecting two unreviewed win-new queue items and running tinker's pre-flight.
verification_pattern.command: grep -q "recommend_cadence_revert" monitor/prompts/poller.md && grep -q "inbound_burst_winnew_unreviewed" monitor/prompts/tinker.md && echo FIXED || echo NOT-IMPLEMENTED

out_of_scope: An enforce phase where an agent flips crons after approval (deferred to a separate future PROP).
Down-throttle / re-quieting logic (the existing manual quiet-period sweep already covers de-escalation; this PROP is up-throttle-on-burst only).
Changing dome-tinker's own cadence (rejected per DIRECTIVE-20260628-001).
counter_arguments: Premature for a 67-day drought? The signal is dormant at zero cost until a burst, and recommendation-only avoids the real risk (an over-eager auto-flip on a single-WIN false alarm). Conservative >=2 threshold + idempotency guard keep false positives near zero.

Two detectors is redundant. Intentional: poller is Sonnet/once-daily and is itself slower under burst (more changes/ to write); tinker is the <=24h safety net. Redundancy is cheap (one metric + one conditional HNOTE).

Why not auto-revert? Auto-flipping crons from an LLM agent is exactly the class of action that caused the 2026-05-21 workspace-sync disaster (LLM improvising an operation under pressure). Recommendation-only is the deliberately conservative first version.
estimated_effort: Small. ~15 lines in poller.md (conditional HNOTE write) + ~6 lines in tinker.md backlog-trend block (one metric + one finding). No new files, no schema/ownership changes.
relationship_to_other_props: Independent of PROP-118 (which addresses WL-3, the poller->analyst ordering gap). Complements PROP-030 (reuses its backlog-trend machinery for detector B). Does not supersede or amend any PROP.

scope: poller.md: added Step 8b (burst-signal HNOTE Detector A). Writes recommend_cadence_revert HNOTE to monitor/decisions/human-notes.json when new_win_delta >= 2. Idempotent on UTC day.
tinker.md: added inbound_burst_winnew_unreviewed metric (Detector B fallback) to PROP-030 metrics block. Emits category:inbound-burst severity:major finding when >= 2 AND poller HNOTE absent in 24h.
Recommendation-only design honored: no automatic cron flipping; operator-control preserved.
Honored PROP-114 dual-write discipline (human-notes.json clone-side write; FUSE rescued by workspace-sync next cycle).
